errors.location: Section 3.9 - Ifa Odu listing (16 main Odu claim, only 8 provided)
errors.currentText: Only 8 Odu listed: EjiOgbe, Oyeku, Iwori, Odi, Irosun, Owonrin, Ogbe, Edi
errors.issue: Template claims '16 个主 Odu 各有完整的神话故事' but only provides details for 8. The missing 8 Odu are: Obara (Ọ̀bàrà), Okanran (Ọ̀kànràn), Ogunda (Ògúndá), Osa (Ọ̀ṣá), Ika (Ìká), Oturupon (Òtúúrúpọ̀n), Otura (Òtúrá), Irete (Ìrẹ̀tẹ̀), Ose (Ọ̀ṣẹ́), Ofun (Òfún). Additionally, 'Edi' is NOT a recognized name in the standard 16 Odu corpus of Yoruba Ifa, and 'Ogbe' (item 7) is either a duplicate of EjiOgbe (item 1) or confused with Ọ̀bàrà.
errors.correctContent: All 16 Odu must be listed with correct Yoruba names: (1) Ogbè/Eji-Ogbe, (2) Ọ̀yẹ̀kú, (3) Ìwòrì, (4) Òdí, (5) Ìrosùn, (6) Ọ̀wọ́nrín, (7) Ọ̀bàrà, (8) Ọ̀kànràn, (9) Ògúndá, (10) Ọ̀ṣá, (11) Ìká, (12) Òtúúrúpọ̀n, (13) Òtúrá, (14) Ìrẹ̀tẹ̀, (15) Ọ̀ṣẹ́, (16) Òfún/Ọ̀ràngún. Remove the non-standard 'Edi' entry and the duplicate 'Ogbe' entry.
errors.source: Wikipedia - Ifa article (UNESCO-recognized 16 Odu corpus); also confirmed by Ifa literary corpus (Ojú Odù) standard

errors.location: Section 3.8 - Tree of Life, 22 Paths example (Tarot mapping)
errors.currentText: 从 Tiphareth(6) 到 Kether(1) 的路径 → 从'整合意识'回归'纯粹意识'——对应塔罗牌是 The Emperor（皇帝），代表'有结构的回归源头'
errors.issue: The path between Tiphareth (6) and Kether (1) is path #3 in the standard Hermetic Qabalah system, corresponding to the Hebrew letter Gimel, associated with The High Priestess (II), NOT The Emperor (IV). The Emperor corresponds to the path between Chokmah (2) and Tiphareth (6) — path #5, Heh.
errors.correctContent: 从 Tiphareth(6) 到 Kether(1) 的路径 → 对应塔罗牌是 The High Priestess（女祭司），代表'通过直觉回归源头'。或者：从 Chokmah(2) 到 Tiphareth(6) 的路径 → 对应塔罗牌是 The Emperor（皇帝），代表'有结构的能量转化'。
errors.source: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn / Aleister Crowley 'Liber 777' — standard path-letter-Tarot correspondences: Gimel (path 13/3) = The High Priestess connects Kether-Tiphareth; Heh (path 15/5) = The Emperor connects Chokmah-Tiphareth

errors.location: Section 3.7 - Gematria systems count (heading vs listing)
errors.currentText: 【三种 Gematria 系统】 followed by 4 numbered items: 1. Standard (Mispar Hechrechi), 2. Mispar Gadol, 3. Mispar Katan, 4. Ordinal Gematria
errors.issue: The heading declares '三种' (three types) but immediately lists FOUR distinct Gematria systems. This is an internal contradiction.
errors.correctContent: Change heading to '【四种 Gematria 系统】' (four types), or restructure to '【主要 Gematria 系统】' (major/primary systems).
errors.source: Internal consistency within the template itself

errors.location: Section 3.1 - Master Numbers (44 as standard master number)
errors.currentText: 44（不约分）：物质大师——在物质世界完全稳定。同时参考 8 的成就能量。
errors.issue: In traditional Pythagorean numerology, the only recognized master numbers are 11, 22, and 33. The number 44 is NOT a standard master number. It is occasionally used in modern extensions but is not part of the foundational system attributed to Pythagoras. Listing 44 alongside 11, 22, 33 as an equally standard master number is misleading.
errors.correctContent: Either remove 44, or clearly annotate it as a modern extension: '44（非标准大师数，部分现代体系使用）：...'
errors.source: Standard Pythagorean numerology texts; Hans Decoz, 'Numerology: Key to the Tarot' (1992); Dan Millman, 'The Life You Were Born to Live' (1993) — only 11, 22, 33 are universally accepted master numbers

errors.currentText: 由全名中的元音（A/E/I/O/U）数值加总得到
errors.issue: In standard Pythagorean numerology, the letter 'Y' is considered a vowel and included in Soul Urge calculation when it produces a vowel sound (e.g., in names like 'Mary', 'Lynn', 'Joyce'). Listing only A, E, I, O, U omits this common rule and will produce incorrect Soul Urge numbers for many names.
errors.correctContent: 由全名中的元音（A/E/I/O/U，以及发音为元音的 Y）数值加总得到
errors.source: Standard numerology texts; Hans Decoz, Tom Monte, 'Numerology: The Complete Guide' (1993); Glynis McCants, 'Glynis Has Your Number' (2006) — all include Y as a vowel in Soul Urge calculation

errors.currentText: 个人年过渡：从 9 到 1 的过渡期（约每年 1-3 月）是最混乱的时期
errors.issue: The Personal Year transition period stated as 'approximately January to March' is only correct for calculations using the calendar year (January-December). However, many numerologists calculate the Personal Year based on birthday-to-birthday cycles instead, in which case the transition occurs around the individual's birthday month, not January. The template should clarify which calculation method is being used.
errors.correctContent: 个人年过渡：从 9 到 1 的过渡期（如按日历年度计算约为每年 1-3 月，如按生日到生日周期计算则为生日前后）是最混乱的时期
errors.source: Decoz 'Numerology: Key to the Tarot' (1992) — discusses both calendar-year and birthday-year methods for Personal Year calculation

errors.currentText: Geburah（5·力量/审判）——限制、审判、勇气
errors.issue: The standard academic transliteration of the Hebrew גבורה is 'Gevurah' (with 'v'), as the letter Beit (ב) without dagesh is pronounced as /v/. The use of 'b' (Geburah) is an older Hermetic/Golden Dawn spelling. While acceptable in Hermetic Qabalistic contexts, it could cause confusion for users familiar with Jewish Kabbalah.
errors.correctContent: Gevurah is the modern standard; 'Geburah' is acceptable as a Hermetic variant but consistent annotation is recommended
errors.source: Jewish Virtual Library 'Gevurah'; Wikipedia 'Tree of Life (Kabbalah)' — both use 'Gevurah'

errors.currentText: Aleph (1), Beth (2), Daleth (4), Heh (5), Kaph (20), Peh (80), Tzaddi (90)
errors.issue: The template uses older transliteration variants (Aleph, Beth, Daleth, Heh, Kaph, Peh, Tzaddi) instead of modern standard forms (Alef, Bet, Dalet, He, Kaf, Pe, Tsadi). While these older forms are common in Hermetic Kabbalistic literature (Crowley, Mathers), they are inconsistent with modern academic and Israeli Hebrew usage. Values themselves are correct.
errors.correctContent: Recommended modern forms: Alef (1), Bet (2), Gimel (3), Dalet (4), He (5), Vav (6), Zayin (7), Chet (8), Tet (9), Yod (10), Kaf (20), Lamed (30), Mem (40), Nun (50), Samekh (60), Ayin (70), Pe (80), Tsadi (90), Qof (100), Resh (200), Shin (300), Tav (400)
errors.source: Wikipedia 'Hebrew Alphabet' — Unicode standard names; Jewish Virtual Library 'Gematria' — both use modern forms

errors.issue: The standard academic transliteration of the Hebrew word בריאה is 'Beri'ah' (three syllables). 'Briah' (two syllables) is a common Hermetic Qabalistic contraction. While widely used, the contracted form loses the middle syllable and differs from the Jewish Kabbalistic pronunciation.
errors.correctContent: Beri'ah is the standard Hebrew form; 'Briah' is acceptable as Hermetic short form
errors.source: Wikipedia 'Four Worlds'; Jewish Kabbalistic texts — standard is 'Beri'ah'

errors.location: Section 3.7 - Gematria value list missing final-form (sofit) letters
errors.currentText: Stops at Tav = 400, with no mention of the five final-form letters Kaf-sofit (ך, 500), Mem-sofit (ם, 600), Nun-sofit (ן, 700), Pe-sofit (ף, 800), Tsadi-sofit (ץ, 900) used in Mispar Gadol system
errors.issue: The Gematria value list only covers the 22 basic letter forms (Aleph through Tav, 1-400). The Mispar Gadol system uses the 5 final-form letters with higher values (500-900). While the template mentions that Gadol involves '终形字母数值更大', it does not list or explain what these final forms and their values are.
errors.correctContent: Add: Kaf-sofit ך = 500, Mem-sofit ם = 600, Nun-sofit ן = 700, Pe-sofit ף = 800, Tsadi-sofit ץ = 900 (used in Mispar Gadol system)
errors.source: Jewish Virtual Library 'Gematria' — discusses final-form letters and their values under Mispar Gadol

errors.location: Section 3.2 - Expression number can stand alone but template says it cannot
errors.currentText: 硬规则：Expression 不单独解读——必须与 Life Path 对照解读
errors.issue: The template states Expression 'must not be interpreted alone'. While Life Path is considered the core number, most standard numerology systems DO interpret Expression number independently in a full reading. The constraint 'must not' is overly rigid and not universally accepted.
errors.correctContent: Expression Number 建议优先与 Life Path 对照解读，但在完整解读中也可以单独提供含义
errors.source: Hans Decoz, Tom Monte 'Numerology: The Complete Guide'; standard practice in professional numerological readings

errors.currentText: 0 → 特殊灵性课题：你面临的是'选择'本身，没有预设方向
errors.issue: The description of Challenge 0 as 'facing the choice itself with no preset direction' is partially accurate, but omits the standard interpretation: Challenge 0 indicates a soul with all options open and unrestricted potential — a 'golden' challenge because it contains all numbers within it. It is also called the 'number of all possibilities' where the person must consciously choose their own path without karmic predisposition.
errors.correctContent: 0 → 特殊灵性课题：所有可能性向你敞开。0 不是缺乏方向，而是包含所有数字的潜能——'无'中蕴含'一切'。你需要自主选择道路，而非被预设方向推动。这是最自由也最需要自觉性的挑战。
errors.source: Decoz 'Numerology: Key to the Tarot'; Hans Decoz, 'Numerology.com Challenge Numbers' articles

errors.location: Section 2 - Data field map, no Pinnacle numbers mentioned
errors.currentText: Only Challenge Numbers mentioned in the data field map and interpretation rules, with no reference to Pinnacle Numbers
errors.issue: In standard Pythagorean numerology, Pinnacle Numbers (周期数) are the paired counterpart of Challenge Numbers. Each of the four life stages has both a Pinnacle (period of growth and opportunity) and a Challenge (period of difficulty to overcome). The template covers Challenges in detail but completely omits the Pinnacle system.
errors.correctContent: Add Pinnacle Numbers as a field in the data map and a corresponding interpretation section. The 4 Pinnacles are calculated as: 1st = Month + Day, 2nd = Day + Year, 3rd = 1st + 2nd, 4th = Month + Year.
errors.source: Hans Decoz 'Pinnacles and Challenges'; standard Pythagorean numerology textbooks

errors.currentText: 10 个源质 listed without any reference to the 11th hidden Sephirah Da'at
errors.issue: The Template of Life section correctly lists the 10 Sephiroth but omits any mention of Da'at (Knowledge, דעת), the invisible/hidden 11th Sephirah that sits between Kether and Tiphareth on the central pillar. Da'at is a crucial concept in Kabbalistic cosmology representing the point where all sefirotic energies become unified in consciousness.
errors.correctContent: Add: Da'at（知识·隐藏的第11源质）——位于中柱 Kether 与 Tiphareth 之间。Da'at 不是独立的源质，而是其他9个源质在意识层面的统一点。当其他源质都平衡时，Da'at 自然出现。
errors.source: Dion Fortune 'The Mystical Qabalah' (1935); Gershom Scholem 'Kabbalah' (1974); standard Kabbalistic texts

errors.location: Section 3.7 - Gematria describes 'Chai = 18 = life' correctly but lacks context on the Chai meaning
errors.currentText: Chai（生命）= Chet(8) + Yod(10) = 18 → 18 = 生命
errors.issue: While the value 18 is correct for Chai (Chet=8, Yod=10), 'Chai' is a transliteration of the Hebrew word חי, not a Chinese word. The template could benefit from establishing the correct Hebrew characters (חי) alongside the transliteration to avoid any ambiguity.
errors.correctContent: The statement is factually correct. Minor recommendation: add Hebrew script: Chai (חי) for clarity.

errors.issue: The template states Birthday Number ranges from 1-31, implying the raw day-of-month number. In standard Pythagorean numerology, Birthday Number is typically reduced to a single digit (1-9) unless it is 11, 22, or 33 (which are kept as-is). The range '1-31' may cause confusion about whether reduction is required.
errors.correctContent: birthday_number：生日数（出生日 1-31，加总到个位数；11/22/33 不约分）
errors.source: Standard Pythagorean numerology practice; Hans Decoz 'Birthday Number' definition

errors.location: Section 1 - Prohibition on mixing Chinese number culture
errors.currentText: 严禁混入：中国数理文化（易经数、五行数等）
errors.issue: While strict separation is a valid design choice, it is worth noting that many modern Chinese numerology apps deliberately synthesize Pythagorean numerology with Chinese number theory. The rigid prohibition is not itself an error, but it limits the template's usefulness for Chinese users who might expect cultural integration.
errors.correctContent: No correction needed — this is a design choice, not an error. Flagged for consideration.
errors.source: N/A — design preference, not factual error

omissions: Complete omission of 8 of the 16 Ifa principal Odu: only EjiOgbe, Oyeku, Iwori, Odi, Irosun, and Owonrin are correctly named; Obara (Ọ̀bàrà), Okanran (Ọ̀kànràn), Ogunda (Ògúndá), Osa (Ọ̀ṣá), Ika (Ìká), Oturupon (Òtúúrúpọ̀n), Otura (Òtúrá), Irete (Ìrẹ̀tẹ̀), Ose (Ọ̀ṣẹ́), Ofun (Òfún) are all absent

No Pinnacle Numbers section — Pinnacles are the paired counterpart to Challenge Numbers and equally important in Pythagorean numerology (4 Pinnacles = 4 life periods of growth, calculated as month+day, day+year, first+second, month+year)
No mention of Karmic Debt Numbers (13, 14, 16, 19) — these are standard in Pythagorean numerology and indicate areas of karmic imbalance that the person must work to resolve
No mention of Da'at (Knowledge, 隐藏的第11源质) — a critical concept in both Jewish Kabbalah and Hermetic Qabalah, representing the hidden unification of the sephirotic energies
No calculation formula for Life Path Number — the template says '由出生日期加总到个位数' but does not explain the exact reduction method (e.g., month+day+year vs. individual reduction method)

No calculation formula for Challenge Numbers — the template lists interpretation rules but never explains HOW the 4 challenges are calculated (1st = |day - month|, 2nd = |year - day|, 3rd = |2nd - 1st|, 4th = |year - month|)
No Pythagorean letter-number mapping chart (A=1, B=2, C=3, ..., Z=8) — essential for understanding how Expression, Soul Urge, and Personality numbers are derived from name letters
No mention of the five sofit (final form) Hebrew letters with their values (500-900) in the Gematria section — essential for Mispar Gadol system understanding
No Birth Day Pinnacle or Essence numbers discussion — these are intermediate concepts in advanced Pythagorean numerology
No corner stones / transit numbers — the template mentions personal year/month/day but not the higher-order time cycles that some systems include
No explanation of the substitution cipher methods in Gematria (Atbash, Atbah, Albam) — the template lists only the four mispar methods but not these important letter-substitution systems
No correlation between Sephiroth and the human body/psyche — standard Kabbalistic interpretations map each Sephirah to a part of the body or a psychological function
No mention of the three veils of negative existence (Ain, Ain Soph, Ain Soph Aur) that precede Kether in the Kabbalistic cosmological model

No Hebrew letter paths mapping to Sephiroth (which path connects which Sephiroth to which) — the template mentions 22 paths and says they correspond to Tarot but does not describe which letters/paths connect which Sephiroth pairs
No discussion of the Qliphoth (the 'shells' or unbalanced/negative aspects of the Tree of Life) — this is a standard component of both Jewish and Hermetic Qabalah
No Ifa Odu binary mark patterns provided (the single/double stroke patterns that define each Odu) — critical for authentic Ifa divination use
No example of how to combine multiple Ifa Odu into a narrative sequence — the template says '如果返回了多个 Odu → 按顺序阅读' but gives no methodology for how to chain them
overallAssessment: The 灵数卡巴拉 (Numerology + Kabbalah) interpretation template is a sophisticated, well-structured document that demonstrates significant understanding of multiple esoteric systems (Pythagorean numerology, Hermetic Qabalah, Jewish Gematria, and Yoruba Ifa). It correctly handles most core numerology concepts (Life Path, Expression, Soul Urge, Personality, Birthday, Personal Year cycles, and Challenge Numbers) with appropriate philosophical framing and anti-hallucination guardrails suitable for AI interpretation. However, it contains several critical errors that reduce its reliability. The most serious issues are in the Ifa section, which claims to cover 16 Odu but only provides 8, includes one non-standard Odu name ('Edi') that does not belong to the standard Ifa corpus of 16, and has a duplicate entry ('Ogbe' redundantly repeating 'EjiOgbe'). In the Kabbalah section, the path-Tarot mapping example is factually wrong — the Kether-to-Tiphareth path corresponds to The High Priestess, not The Emperor. The Gematria section has an internal contradiction (saying 'three' systems but listing four). Additionally, the template omits the paired Pinnacle Number system, Karmic Debt numbers, the hidden 11th Sephirah Da'at, and the final-form Hebrew letters (sofit) essential for Mispar Gadol. The Personal Year transition assumption of January-March is stated without acknowledging birthday-based alternatives. The Soul Urge calculation omits 'Y' as a vowel. Master Number 44 is presented as standard when only 11, 22, 33 are universally recognized. The template uses older Hermetic transliterations (Geburah, Tiphareth, Kether, Briah, etc.) which are acceptable for the Hermetic Qabalah tradition but inconsistent with academic standards. Overall, the template is well-conceived for its intended purpose and usable with corrections to the Ifa section (the most critical area needing revision) and the path-Tarot mapping error. For a production AI divination tool, addressing the high-severity errors is essential before deployment.
